title: Tareas matemáticas abiertas como respuesta didáctica a la inteligencia artificial generativa en contextos post-IA
extended_summary:
This paper examines a didactic problem created by the widespread availability of generative AI in school mathematics: many traditional tasks can now be solved automatically, which may reduce students’ interpretation, decision-making, and validation work. The author asks how mathematics teaching can preserve students’ mathematical activity and epistemic control in so-called post-AI contexts.

To address this issue, the paper analyzes a classroom experience in secondary education in which open mathematical tasks were implemented as a response to generative AI. The tasks were mediated by a didactic regulation device called COMPAS, which structures activity into phases such as understanding the situation, organizing assumptions and data, mathematical modeling, producing and exploring results, analyzing and validating, and socializing/synthesizing. The study uses a qualitative, descriptive-interpretive approach and examines student written work, classroom interactions, and teacher-researcher observations.

The context is a secondary school mathematics classroom in Peru. Students worked on open-ended tasks intentionally designed without explicit numerical data or closed instructions, so that they had to formulate assumptions, model the situation, and validate results rather than rely on direct computation. AI could be used as a partial support tool, but only after students had made key mathematical decisions.

The paper concludes that open tasks, when paired with explicit didactic regulation, can sustain meaningful mathematical activity even in the presence of generative AI. Students retained epistemic control, with AI functioning as a subordinate resource for exploration or checking rather than as a source of final answers. The author argues that task design and regulation are central to preserving the formative value of school mathematics in post-AI settings and suggests further research on applying COMPAS in other grade levels, content areas, and teacher education settings.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative, descriptive-interpretive classroom study, not an experimental or quasi-experimental impact evaluation. It provides useful practice-based evidence, but credibility for causal inference is limited by the single setting, small scope, and lack of comparison group.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests meaningful pedagogical value for sustaining mathematical agency in post-IA contexts, but it reports no quantitative effect sizes or comparative outcomes. Impact is therefore plausible but unclear in magnitude and generalizability.

interventions.use_case: Use of open mathematical tasks in secondary mathematics classrooms, mediated by the didactic regulation device COMPAS, to structure how generative AI can be used as a support tool while preserving student mathematical agency and epistemic control.

finding.finding_summary: This qualitative secondary-school classroom study reports that open mathematical tasks, combined with explicit didactic regulation via COMPAS, helped students maintain epistemic control over mathematical activity even when generative AI was available. The paper does not report an effect size, but it describes students actively formulating assumptions, building models, and validating solutions rather than delegating the task to AI.
finding.measure: Student mathematical activity, model construction, and validation practices observed through written work, classroom interactions, and teacher observations

finding.finding_summary: The study finds that the task design supported student agency, decision-making, and critical validation of AI-generated or AI-supported results. Students compared models, justified assumptions, and negotiated plausibility criteria, indicating strengthened metacognitive and critical-thinking practices in the mathematics classroom.
finding.measure: Observed student agency, argumentation, and critical validation behaviors during task resolution
